flowSteps: Select the vaccine. Use a WHO EPI preset; enter custom parameters only from a reliable source.
Read the VVM on the vial and select its stage.
Enter each temperature exposure as an interval (temperature and duration). If a freeze-sensitive vaccine was at 0 °C or below, do a shake test and select the result.
Read the verdict, the reasons and the recommended action. Save or share the result for your report.
help.safetyTitle: The calculation never decides the verdict
help.safetyDesc: The verdict comes only from what you check on the vial: the VVM and, after freezing, the shake test. The MKT and potency estimate are reference values for reporting. If you are unsure, do not use the vaccine and ask your supervisor.
decisionSteps: VVM at stage 3 or 4 → Discard, whatever the calculation shows.
Freeze-sensitive vaccine (❄️🚫) exposed to 0 °C or below → shake test required. Failed → Discard. Not done → Hold.
VVM not checked → Hold. Read the VVM first; if the vial has no VVM, ask your supervisor.
help.verdictTitle: What to do with each verdict

verdictList.desc: Administer following standard protocol. If a VVM is at stage 2, use that vial first.
Keep the vial in the cold chain at its recommended temperature, label it "Do not use", complete the missing check (VVM reading or shake test), then assess again.
Do not use the vial. Record the disposal and report it to your supervisor.

vvmList.desc: Inner square lighter than the outer circle. Usable.
Inner square darker, but still lighter than the circle. Usable; use these vials before stage 1 vials.
Inner square the same colour as the circle. Discard point: do not use.
Inner square darker than the circle. Do not use.

help.vvmNote: The VVM records cumulative heat exposure only. It does not show freezing damage or the expiry date, so check those separately.
help.shakeTitle: How to do a shake test
shakeSteps: Make a control: take a vial of the same vaccine, manufacturer and batch. Freeze it until the contents are completely solid, then let it thaw.
Hold the control and the suspect vial together and shake them vigorously for about 10–15 seconds.
Put both vials side by side on a flat surface and watch them.
If the suspect vial settles more slowly than the control, it passed. If it settles at the same speed or faster, it failed: discard it.
Test one vial from each exposed batch. If the suspect vial is still frozen, do not use it.
help.intervalDesc: Enter each period at a different temperature as one interval (up to 10). Include the time back in normal storage if you want a complete record.
help.estimateTitle: What the MKT and potency estimate mean
help.estimateDesc: MKT (mean kinetic temperature) combines several temperatures into one equivalent temperature, giving more weight to hot periods. The potency estimate applies an Arrhenius model to the MKT. The model parameters for each vaccine are not yet validated, so both values are for reporting and for discussion with your supervisor, not for deciding whether to use the vaccine.

termList.desc: A single constant temperature equivalent to a series of varying temperatures, weighted toward hot periods (WHO TRS 961, Annex 9).
A heat-sensitive label on the vial that changes colour with cumulative heat exposure.
A comparison with a deliberately frozen control vial that shows whether an adsorbed vaccine has been damaged by freezing.
Vaccines damaged by freezing, such as DTP and hepatitis B. They must never be frozen.
Model parameters: how strongly the degradation rate depends on temperature (activation energy), and the degradation rate at a reference temperature.

help.customDesc: Only enter Ea, k_ref and reference temperature from a reliable source, such as the manufacturer's data sheet or WHO documents. Custom parameters affect only the reference estimate, not the verdict.
help.shareDesc: Save Record keeps the result on this device. Share opens your device's share menu (WhatsApp, email, messages); where that is not available, the summary is copied so you can paste it. The shared text lists the verdict, the reasons and the recommended action.
help.dataDesc: Assessment history is stored only in this browser's local storage on this device. Nothing is sent to a server.
